definition: Upbraid means to criticize or scold severely.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word upbraid. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know upbraid should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: The head librarian upbraided the volunteers for shelving by color, and the lecture outlasted the mistake by an hour.
Scold is milder than upbraid — quicker, hotter, and over by dinner.
Excoriate is fiercer than upbraid: an upbraiding is a severe telling-off, while to excoriate is to take the hide off entirely.

A reprimand is an official scolding — often written, often on the record, its weight borrowed from the office behind it. To upbraid is personal and wordy: a severe, itemized telling-off delivered face to face. A reprimand can be one cold paragraph in a file; an upbraiding lists every fault aloud.

A rebuke is a sharp expression of disapproval — usually one stern sentence that marks the fault and stops. To upbraid is to keep going: a sustained, detailed scolding that walks through the offense point by point. A rebuke stings once; an upbraiding is a lecture.
